summary: This re-adopts PR #618's fix for a real, self-identified bug in the previous RLS migration: SELECT-only policies on prompt_translations/prompt_localizations/prompt_marketplace_listings would have silently blocked every INSERT/UPDATE from app_runtime (a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role) despite table-level GRANTs permitting those operations, since Postgres RLS still applies on top of GRANTs. The migration file (drizzle/0268, still unapplied live, per this repo's tier2 convention) correctly replaces the SELECT-only policies with FOR ALL / USING(true) / WITH CHECK(true) policies and adds the missing UPDATE grants for app_runtime on the two tables that lacked them; I traced the DROP/CREATE/GRANT sequence end to end and the final state is internally consistent, idempotent, and free of naming collisions with the existing 265-entry migration journal. The bundled feature work (prompt translation/localization/marketplace/export-import services, schema, API routes, and a browse UI) that this fix rides along with follows established codebase conventions throughout: requireAuth() on every route, ServiceError-based error mapping, veridian_admin gating via permission-service.ts consistent with every other Prompt OS write action, and the same platform-wide (non-tenant, attribution-only orgId) posture already used for prompt_templates/prompt_versions and workerAgents. I read the full source of all four new services (not just their tests, which were cut off in the supplied diff) and did not find correctness or security defects; the lack of per-org ownership checks on publish/unlist is intentional and matches the existing platform-wide admin model, not a new regression. I could not independently run bun test or tsc in this review environment (no bun/node_modules present) so the worker's reported 27/27 test pass and clean tsc are not independently re-verified, and this diff does not touch .github/workflows/** so the hard workflow-scope rule is not implicated. Given the diff touches *.sql/schema/rls paths, tier2 applies as expected -- this is ready for human sign-off, not autonomous merge.
